original_sql:
SELECT p.payment_id, p.customer_id, p.amount
FROM payment p
WHERE p.amount > (SELECT AVG(p2.amount) FROM payment p2 WHERE p2.customer_id = p.customer_id)

candidates.sql:
SELECT p.payment_id, p.customer_id, p.amount
FROM payment p
JOIN (
    SELECT customer_id, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount
    FROM payment
    GROUP BY customer_id
) c ON p.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE p.amount > c.avg_amount
candidates.rationale: Replaces the correlated subquery with a derived table that computes the average amount per customer once, then joins it to the main table, avoiding repeated subquery execution.

FROM payment p
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM payment p2
    WHERE p2.customer_id = p.customer_id

)
AND p.amount > (SELECT AVG(p2.amount) FROM payment p2 WHERE p2.customer_id = p.customer_id)
candidates.rationale: Adds an EXISTS check to quickly filter out rows where no payment in the same customer group is less than the current amount, potentially reducing the number of rows for which the average subquery is evaluated.
